title: When to Rebid Your Office Cleaning Contract (Cycle Timing & Benchmarks)
seoTitle: When to Rebid Contract: Office Cleaning RFP Frequency & Cost Guide
metaDescription: Learn when to rebid contract terms for commercial office cleaning (24-36 months vs annual) to stop 4-7% CPI creep. Benchmark rates in our cost calculator.
excerpt: Rebidding a commercial janitorial contract every 12 months creates high crew turnover and startup friction, while letting contracts auto-renew past 36 months invites 12% to 22% price creep. Discover the optimal 2-plus-1 rebid cycle and the five operational triggers that justify an immediate RFP.
quickAnswer: For most US commercial offices (2,500 to 50,000+ sq ft), the optimal window for when to rebid contract agreements is every 24 to 36 months—structured as a 2-year initial term with one performance-gated 1-year renewal option. Rebidding on a 3-year cycle prevents compound CPI price escalations from pushing your rates above national benchmarks ($0.07 to $0.15 per sq ft per visit) while giving incumbent contractors enough amortization stability to invest in commercial equipment and retain background-checked night crews.

blocks.text: The Strategic Sweet Spot: Why 24 to 36 Months Beats Annual Rebidding

Determining when to rebid contract terms for commercial office cleaning requires balancing two opposing economic forces: vendor complacency and mobilization friction. When facility managers leave an incumbent janitorial company on evergreen auto-renewal for four to six years, annual Consumer Price Index (CPI) or minimum-wage pass-through escalators of 3.5% to 6% compound rapidly. Meanwhile, hybrid office attendance shifts or department consolidations often reduce actual soil loads without any corresponding downward adjustment in billed labor hours. By Year 4, a 15,000-square-foot office that should pay $2,273 to $3,897 per month for 5x-week service ($0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft per visit across 21.65 monthly visits) is routinely overpaying by $450 to $900 per month.

Conversely, corporate procurement teams that force a mandatory full RFP every 12 months suffer from chronic transition fatigue. Onboarding a new janitorial contractor requires issuing security badges, background-checking night cleaners, auditing Certificates of Insurance (COI), re-labeling chemical closets under OSHA HazCom, and enduring a 30- to 45-day learning curve while crews memorize light switches, alarm codes, and executive areas. Furthermore, reputable contractors amortize their startup equipment investments—such as HEPA backpack vacuums, compact auto-scrubbers, and proportioning stations—over 24 to 36 months. If your RFP signals a strict 1-year term, top-tier vendors add a 6% to 10% startup risk premium to their square-foot rate.

blocks.title: The '2+1+1' Commercial Janitorial Contract Structure
blocks.text: Institutional property managers (BOMA Class A and corporate campuses) overwhelmingly favor a 24-month base contract with two unilateral 12-month renewal options held solely by the client—requiring a full market rebid or benchmark audit at Month 36.
Comparing Rebid Cycles Across Office Size Brackets

The right rebid cadence also depends on your facility's square footage, service frequency ( calculated at 4.33 weeks per month), and special flooring or security complexity. Smaller suites have near-zero equipment amortization barriers, whereas multi-floor facilities rely heavily on site-specific mechanized floor equipment and dedicated evening supervisors.

blocks.text: 5 Early Triggers That Mean You Should Rebid Before Contract Expiration

Even if you are only 14 months into a planned 36-month cycle, five operational or financial red flags signal that you should prepare a mid-cycle RFP and exercise your 30-day termination-for-convenience or cure-notice clause:

items: 1. Unverifiable Labor Hours & Ghost Shifts: Electronic badge swipe logs or alarm arm/disarm timestamps reveal the night crew is spending 2.5 total labor hours in a 20,000 sq ft office that was bid and billed at 5.7 labor hours per night (based on the ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hr benchmark at $35 to $65/hr).

2. Revolving-Door Cleaner Turnover (>3x in 6 Months): When your account manager cycles through three different night crews in six months without delivering updated background checks or site orientation, supervisor oversight has collapsed—and security risks skyrocket.

3. Occupancy or Hybrid Schedule Contraction (+/- 25% Headcount): If your company shifts to a 3-day in-office hybrid schedule or subleases half a floor, switching from 5x-week service (21.65 visits/mo, 0.90 frequency multiplier) to 3x-week service (13.0 visits/mo, 0.95 multiplier) with low-use zone rotation should reduce monthly spend by 25% to 35%. If the incumbent refuses to right-size the scope, go to market.

4. Uncapped Escalation Demands Above 4% CPI: If an incumbent demands an 8% to 12% mid-term rate hike citing general labor inflation without opening their payroll books or state prevailing/minimum wage statutes, competitive bidding is the only reliable check.

5. Chronic Restroom & Consumable Stockouts: Repeated Monday-morning complaints about empty dispensers, sour mop odors on ceramic tile and grout (1.12 multiplier), or skipped quarterly deep floor care ($0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month) indicate the vendor is under-staffing your building to subsidize other accounts.

blocks.text: How to Decouple Restroom Dispensers and Consumables Before Rebidding

One subtle reason facility managers delay rebidding an underperforming janitorial contractor is 'dispenser lock-in.' Some vendors install proprietary leased soap and paper dispensers at the start of a contract; if you fire the contractor, they threaten to strip every dispenser off your restroom walls or charge an inflated buyout fee. Before you launch your next RFP, standardize your restrooms with facility-owned, universal or high-efficiency commercial fixtures so any incoming janitorial bidder can restock them without hardware disruption.

For example, owning your wall-mounted Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam 1100 mL Touchless Soap Dispenser units (ADA-compliant, delivering up to 2,750 handwashes per refill on a 3-year battery life) ensures consistent hygiene regardless of who holds the labor contract. Likewise, specifying universal-fit consumable skus in your RFP—such as Tork Universal Multifold Hand Towels Natural (16-Pack Case of 4,000 100%-recycled sheets measuring 9.125 x 9.5 inches) and Tork Universal Jumbo Bath Tissue 2-Ply (12-Case of 9-inch diameter, 1,000-foot EcoLogo-certified rolls)—allows you to benchmark the consumables add-on ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit) transparently across all competing bidders.
90-Day Countdown Timeline for a Zero-Disruption Contract Rebid

items.name: Day -90: Audit Current Notice Window and Actual Net Cleanable Sq Ft
items.text: Pull your existing contract to verify the non-renewal notice deadline (typically 30 or 60 days prior to anniversary) and verify net cleanable square footage by flooring type (carpet 1.0x, VCT 1.04x, tile/grout 1.12x, polished concrete 0.95x).

items.name: Day -75: Issue Standardized Task-and-Frequency RFP to 4 Bidders
items.text: Invite three pre-qualified external commercial janitorial contractors plus the incumbent (if performance is acceptable but pricing is high) to bid on an identical production-hour and deliverable worksheet.

items.name: Day -50: Conduct Mandatory Group or Scored Site Walkthroughs
items.text: Walk every bidder through the exact office zones, breakrooms ($12 to $25/visit add-on), interior glass partitions ($15 to $35/visit add-on), and janitor closet slop sink setup so no vendor can claim surprise post-award.

items.name: Day -30: Award Contract, Issue Termination Notice, and Verify COI
items.text: Deliver formal written notice to the outgoing vendor, collect the incoming contractor's Certificate of Insurance (general liability, workers' comp, and janitorial fidelity bond), and schedule a 14-day security badge and key handover.

faqs.q: Should we tell our incumbent cleaning company that we are putting the contract out to bid?
faqs.a: Yes—unless you are terminating them for cause (theft, safety violations, or severe breach). When an incumbent with decent day-to-day performance knows a formal 3-year market rebid is underway, they frequently sharpen their pencil by 5% to 12%, refresh site equipment, and assign a senior area manager to retain the account without forcing you through a crew transition.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to rebid a commercial office cleaning contract?
faqs.a: Mid-spring (April–May) and early autumn (September–October) are ideal. Avoid transitioning janitorial vendors in late November through February in snow-belt markets, when entrance matting, rock salt removal, and holiday party cleanups peak, and avoid December 31 effective dates when insurance renewals and corporate holiday shutdowns delay security badge processing.

faqs.q: Can we benchmark prices without conducting a full formal RFP every two years?
faqs.a: Yes. During Year 2 of a 2+1 contract, you can conduct an internal 'Should-Cost Audit' using ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hr production standards, local hourly billing rates ($35 to $65/hr standard), and 4.33 weeks/month visit math. If the incumbent's requested renewal increase stays within 2% to 3% of the calculated market benchmark and QA scores exceed 90%, exercising the 1-year renewal option saves ~25 hours of procurement administration.

faqs.q: What notice period should we require in a new commercial cleaning agreement?
faqs.a: Always negotiate a bilateral 30-day 'Termination for Convenience' clause (or unilateral 30-day client termination right) paired with a 15-day 'Termination for Cause' cure window, regardless of whether the base contract term is 12, 24, or 36 months. Never sign an agreement that locks you in without a 30-day exit ramp.
